slo_title: Define the core principles of functional programming

mcq.q: In which paradigm is recursion preferred over loops for iteration?
In functional programming, a function is said to be "pure" if it:

options.C: C) Has no side effects and returns the same output for the same input

mcq.answer_text: C) Has no side effects and returns the same output for the same input

mcq.q: Which of the following is a core principle of functional programming?
Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of functional programming?
What is the main difference between functional and imperative programming paradigms?

options.A: A) Imperative focuses on what to solve; Functional focuses on how to solve
options.B: B) Functional uses variables and loops extensively
options.C: C) Functional emphasizes immutability and pure functions, while imperative relies on changing state and control flow
options.D: D) Both paradigms are fundamentally the same

mcq.answer_text: C) Functional emphasizes immutability and pure functions, while imperative relies on changing state and control flow

sq.q: In what way does functional programming differ from imperative programming when summing a list of numbers?
answer: Functional uses recursion or reduce() without mutable state; imperative uses loops and updates variables.

sq.q: A company wants to reduce bugs in their payroll software. Why should they consider functional programming?
answer: Functional programming avoids side effects and uses pure functions, making the code predictable and easier to test
